title: High-throughput papain-based DNA extraction from whole invertebrates
author: Rosa Whittingham
materials: Wash Buffer 1 should be comprised of the following reagents: A B C D 1 Reagent Required concentration in buffer Chemical molarity Amount per 100 mL 2 Guanidine HCl 7 M 95.53 29.4 g 3 Ethanol 56 % - 56 mL 4 H2O - - 44 mL

steps.title: Collect and preserve specimens
steps.instruction: Collect individual invertebrates from the field into 100 % ethanol, cleaning all collection equipment with Chemgene or diluted bleach between samples and following all permitting and ethical guidelines. Store the ethanol‑preserved specimens at –20 °C until processing.

steps.title: Grind frozen specimens
steps.instruction: Remove specimens from –20 °C storage, place them in a Geno/Grinder 2010 and grind at full speed (1750 RPM) for 2 minutes (or 4 minutes for larvae). If the material is not fully homogenised, repeat the grinding step.

steps.title: Optional pre‑freeze for brittleness
steps.instruction: Freeze the samples overnight at –20 °C (or at –80 °C for more efficient grinding, ensuring the plasticware can tolerate the temperature).

steps.title: Prepare lysis buffers
steps.instruction: Make Lysis Buffer 1 (pH 9) containing per 100 mL: 58.44 g NaCl (120 mM), 5 mL 1 M Tris‑HCl (50 mM), 4 mL 0.5 M EDTA (20 mM), and 91 mL water. Make Lysis Buffer 2 (pH 9) with the same components plus 3 g SDS (3 %). Prepare Elution Buffer (pH ≈ 7) with per 100 mL: 1 mL 1 M Tris‑HCl (10 mM) and 99 mL water. Prepare Wash Buffer 1 (composition not specified) and Wash Buffer 2 (pH ≈ 7) containing per 100 mL: 70 mL ethanol (70 % v/v, 58.44 g), 1 mL 1 M Tris‑HCl (10 mM), and 29 mL water.

steps.title: Add lysis reagents and papain
steps.instruction: To each ground sample add 140 µL Lysis Buffer 1, 60 µL Lysis Buffer 2 and 20 µL 100 mg mL⁻¹ papain (ten‑fold the concentration of standard Proteinase K). Vortex briefly to mix.

steps.title: Incubate for protein digestion
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture at 37 °C overnight (12–16 h) to inactivate proteins (alternatively, incubate at 56 °C for 3 h).

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate at 4 000 g for 2 minutes, remove ball bearings with a magnet, then centrifuge at 4 000 g for 4 minutes. Transfer 1 mL of the supernatant to a clean 2.2 mL deep‑well 96‑well plate for archiving and retain the remainder in the original plate.

steps.title: Secondary clarification
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the remaining lysate at 2 000 g for 4 minutes, then transfer 200 µL of the clarified supernatant to a new 2.2 mL deep‑well plate. Store any leftover lysate at –20 °C for future use.

steps.title: Prepare Protein Denaturation master mix
steps.instruction: Make Protein Denaturation Buffer (per 100 mL: 47.7 g Guanidine HCl, 5 M; add water to 100 mL). For each 96‑well plate prepare a master mix of 1 : 1 Protein Denaturation Buffer and 100 % ethanol. Two volume sets are reported: 220 µL of each component per sample (total 42.2 mL buffer and 42.2 µL ethanol per plate) and alternatively 220 µL of each per sample (total 21.1 mL buffer and 21.1 µL ethanol per plate). Use whichever matches your plate format.

steps.title: Add denaturation mix to lysate
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL of the supernatant from the previous step into each well containing the Protein Denaturation Buffer‑ethanol master mix, or add 400 µL of the master mix directly to each well of a 2.2 mL 96‑well plate, depending on the chosen volume scheme.

steps.title: Load sample onto spin column
steps.instruction: Add the entire sample solution (~600 µL) to a well of a 96‑well DNA membrane spin column, cover with a breathable seal, and place the column plate over a suitable reservoir (e.g., a 2.2 mL deep‑well plate).

steps.title: First spin and discard flow‑through
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at ≥6 000 × g for 1 minute (if the centrifuge cannot reach 6 000 × g, extend to 10 minutes). Discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: Wash with Buffer 1
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL Wash Buffer 1 to each spin column, cover with a breathable seal, then centrifuge at ≥6 000 × g for 1 minute (or 5 minutes if the speed is lower). Discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: Wash with Buffer 2
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL Wash Buffer 2 to each spin column, cover with a breathable seal, then centrifuge at 20 000 × g for 3 minutes (or 15 minutes if the speed is lower). Discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: Final high‑speed spin
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the column at ≥20 000 × g for 3 minutes (or 15 minutes if the centrifuge cannot reach this speed) to remove residual ethanol.

steps.title: Transfer to elution plate
steps.instruction: Carefully move the spin‑column plate onto a new 0.5 mL DNA collection plate, ensuring the liquid level does not touch the membrane to avoid ethanol carry‑over.

steps.title: Elute DNA
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL Elution Buffer directly onto the silica membrane, cover with a breathable seal, and incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Collect eluted DNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at ≥6 000 × g for 1 minute (or 2 minutes if speed is lower). The DNA is now in the collection plate and can be used for downstream amplification. Steps of adding Elution Buffer and centrifugation may be repeated to increase yield, noting that overall concentration will be lower.

steps.title: Prepare carbon steel beads (optional)
steps.instruction: Add one 3 mm hardened carbon‑steel bead to each well of a 1.2 mL 96‑well plate. To remove manufacturing oil, place beads in a glass beaker and bake at 250 °C for at least 12 hours. Vortex samples briefly to ensure thorough mixing before downstream applications.

steps.title: Sterilise glassware for buffers
steps.instruction: Acid‑wash borosilicate bottles with ~100 mL 0.4 M HCl, neutralise with ~100 mL 0.4 M NaHCO₃ (33.604 g NaHCO₃ per 1 L water), then rinse twice with ~100 mL water before preparing buffers.
